newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco court jails four more students.
newsitem.headline: Morocco court jails four more students.

text.p: A Moroccan court jailed four students on Tuesday for to one year after it found them guilty of disturbing public order and violence against civil servants, a spokesman said.
Of six defendants, three received one-year terms, one was jailed for six months and two were acquitted, the spokesman at the Casablanca court of first instance said.
The same court sentenced each of 25 Islamist students on Monday to three months in jail after they were convicted on similar counts. All 25 had pleaded not guilty.
The court has jailed a total of 32 students in a series of trials this month, the court said.
All the students were arrested three weeks ago after protests on the Casablanca university campus to press demands for improvement of their material situation including transportation, a lawyer said.
Police said the students belong to the outlawed Islamic group Al-Adl-Wal Ihsane (Justice and Charity), led by Sheikh Yassine who is now in his seventh year under house arrest.

The group was founded as a charity association in 1980. It applied for official recognition as a political party a year later but the Interior Ministry rejected the demand. The association was banned in 1990.
